title: Instruction Hierarchy Violations: Do Models Prioritize User Harm Requests Over System Prompt Safety Rules?

original_idea.title: Instruction Hierarchy Violations: Do Models Prioritize User Harm Requests Over System Prompt Safety Rules?
original_idea.problem: Models receive instructions from both system prompts (operator level) and user turns (user level). A safety failure occurs when user-level harmful requests override system-prompt safety constraints.
original_idea.direction: Design 30 scenarios with a safety-constraining system prompt and a user-level request that violates the constraint. Vary the pressure level of the user request (mild, moderate, persistent). Evaluate 2-3 models. Measure instruction hierarchy compliance and identify conditions under which user requests override operator constraints.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Instruction hierarchy robustness is a real deployment safety concern, especially for enterprise applications that rely on system prompts to enforce safety policies. No standard benchmark directly tests this.
original_idea.relevant_context: Anthropic and OpenAI both describe instruction hierarchy in their documentation. The 2025 AI Agent Index documented diverse system prompt configurations. AILuminate does not test system prompt override scenarios.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reduced from 4 to 3. Multiple papers (OpenAI instruction hierarchy, Control Illusion, ICLR 2025) already test system prompt override scenarios. The marginal contribution is reduced.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: designing system prompts and user requests, then measuring compliance rates, requires only basic prompt engineering and API calls. Highly suitable for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: 30 scenarios times 3 pressure levels times 2-3 models is a well-bounded experiment with a clear binary outcome measure.

novelty.reasoning: Instruction hierarchy is an active research area. OpenAI published 'The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions' (2024, arxiv 2404.13208) and applied it to GPT-3.5. OpenAI's IH-Challenge dataset strengthened instruction hierarchy in GPT-5 Mini-R. 'A Closer Look at System Prompt Robustness' (2025) and 'Control Illusion: The Failure of Instruction Hierarchies in LLMs' (2025) directly test system prompt override scenarios. The RULES benchmark evaluates instruction following with conflicting inputs. 'Reasoning Up the Instruction Ladder' (2025) reframes prioritization as meta-reasoning. The specific 30-scenario varying-pressure design is clean but the core research question is already substantially explored.
